Roofing in Frisco, Texas

Frisco's roofs went up fast, and hail keeps finding them. Learn how the city checks contractors, then call one free number at any hour to reach an independent roofing company that works in Frisco.

Call (469) 649-7066 Check a roofer's R-Number

  3. Frisco

A city that grew six times over in twenty years

Frisco counted about 33,700 residents in the 2000 census, about 117,000 in 2010 and 200,509 in 2020. It sits in two counties, Collin and Denton, and much of its housing went up during those two decades.

For roofing in Frisco TX, that timeline matters more than any single storm. Homes finished in the early 2000s have now carried their shingles through twenty or more North Texas summers. Homes from the 2010s may already have a second roof because hail forced it. Either way, a large share of Frisco owners are buying a roof for the first time, and they are doing it in a city with clear rules about who can do the work.

DFW Expert Roofers is a free line, not a roofer. Call it, explain the problem, and you are transferred to an independent, owner-run roofing company that serves Frisco. That company sees the roof, prices it and does the job.

The Frisco R-Number, and why it is worth asking for

Frisco requires every contractor to register before it gets a permit. The registration carries a detail most cities do not spell out.

  1. The roofer registers online. Registration goes through eTRAKiT, the city's permit system, with company and contact details and the registration fee.
  2. Insurance comes first. The roofer sends a general liability certificate with the City of Frisco listed as holder. Until the documents arrive, the registration stays pending.
  3. The city issues an R-Number. That number lapses on the date the roofer's general liability policy ends. A lapsed policy means a lapsed registration.
  4. The permit follows. The city tells contractors to confirm their registration status before applying, since a permit is not issued to an unregistered contractor.

Ask any roofer for its Frisco R-Number and the expiration date on its liability certificate. If the two do not line up, or the roofer cannot produce either, keep looking.

Same shingle or something new: two permit paths

Self-service permit

The city's residential permit list includes a self-service permit for a roof replaced with the same material. A registered contractor gets it right away online, so it should not hold up a job.

Reviewed permit

Roof work that changes things, such as a different material, goes through the city's electronic plan review. Allow time for it, and ask the roofer to include it in the schedule it gives you.

Many Frisco subdivisions also have an HOA that approves roof colors and materials. Get the association's approval in writing before the permit goes in, so a crew is never waiting on a form. Keep the permit and final inspection records with the roof warranty.

Wind, not just hail

The 2017 storm is a reminder that straight-line wind does real harm here. Wind lifts shingle tabs, loosens ridge caps and works at chimney flashing, and the damage is easy to miss from the street. After a windy night, walk the yard for shingle pieces and look at the ceilings inside.

Check how your homeowners policy treats the roof before the next storm. Ask your agent whether roof damage is paid at replacement cost or actual cash value, what the hail and wind deductible is, and how long you have to report a claim.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Why Frisco owners call

The builder roof is tired

A house from Frisco's early boom years is on its original shingles, with granules in the gutters and curling edges.

Hail swept the neighborhood

Trucks and yard signs appear the morning after. The owner would rather choose a roofer than wait for a knock.

A change of material

Impact-resistant shingles or metal mean a reviewed permit and an HOA form, so timing and paperwork matter.

A leak after wind

A ceiling stain or a drip near a vent after a gusty storm, and the owner wants someone to look before it spreads.

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

Frisco roofing questions

Do roofing contractors have to register in Frisco TX?

Yes. Frisco says every contractor working in the city must be registered with its Building Inspections Division before a permit is issued. Registration is done online in eTRAKiT and requires a general liability certificate listing the City of Frisco as the holder. The city then issues an R-Number that runs out on the insurance expiration date.

Is a permit required to reroof a Frisco house?

Plan on one. The city lists a self-service residential permit for a roof replaced with the same material, which a registered contractor can get right away online. A change, such as a different roofing material, goes through electronic review instead. Ask your roofer which kind your job needs and for a copy once it is issued.

What should I look for in Frisco roofing contractors?

A current Frisco R-Number, a liability certificate that matches it, a written estimate naming the shingle and underlayment, and a plan for the permit. Ask how bad decking is priced and what is paid up front. Texas does not license roofers, so these documents matter. Our guide on checking a Texas roofer goes further.

Does hail really hit Frisco that often?

Often enough to plan for it. The National Weather Service logged golf ball hail that damaged a roof near Legacy Drive and SH 121 in April 2014, WFAA reported hail up to baseball size between Frisco and McKinney in March 2019, and the Weather Service placed some of the March 2024 storm's largest hail near Frisco and Prosper. See hail damage roof repair.

Is DFW Expert Roofers a roofing company in Frisco?

No. It is a free phone line. Day or night, an automated assistant answers, then transfers you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that serves Frisco. That company inspects, prices the work, handles the permit and the work, and the bill comes from it, not the line. A connected roofer may pay the line for referrals.
